text:
maria: Heads up — hitting a gnarly TS + edge runtime issue in the new sample app. SDK generics are getting erased and users see `any` at runtime / compile-time type mismatch when bundling for edge functions. Repro in `samples/edge-ts` with latest SDK.
kevin: can you paste a minimal repro + tsconfig? that helps.
maria: sure — stripped down:
```ts
// samples/edge-types/src/edge.ts
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference';

const c = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });

export default async function handler(req: Request) {
  const embeddings = await c.embed<string[]>({ input: 'hello' });
  // TS expects string[], but editors & runtime show any[] / unknown[]
  return new Response(JSON.stringify({ first: embeddings[0] }));
}
```
tsconfig:
```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2020",
    "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "node",
    "isolatedModules": true,
    "esModuleInterop": false,
    "skipLibCheck": false,
    "declaration": true
  }
}
```
maria: build error is subtle — tsc emits declarations from our SDK's overloads that confuse `isolatedModules` in Vite/ESBuild or the edge bundler. Also some folks hit `default import` vs `import * as` errors unless esModuleInterop is on.
jon: this lines up with what I saw — the SDK used a bunch of overload signatures for `embed(...)` and `generate(...)` to support different input shapes. With `isolatedModules` / transpilers, overload-only patterns sometimes result in a fallback to `any` in downstream inference of generics.
jon: quick notes:
- overload order matters for inference; TS will often pick the first compatible overload which can be too broad
- declaration emit with `declaration: true` can expose conditional types that bundlers don't preserve
- `esModuleInterop: true` usually hides the default-import issues for consumers
kevin: options:
1) change typings to a single generic-based signature (one broad generic T = unknown) instead of many overloads so inference flows consistently
2) publish a smaller typedeclaration patch that narrows exported types and adds `// @internal` to internal helpers so they don't leak
3) update sample tsconfig to recommend `esModuleInterop: true`, `skipLibCheck: true` for now
sophie: I'm +1 for (1). Overloads gave us fine DX historically, but for the SDK surface area (many targets: Node ESM, CJS, edge) a single generic with constrained helpers is more robust. I'll draft a PR to replace key overloads with a single generic signature and keep backward compat via JSDoc/compat types.
sophie: proposed signature (sketch):
```ts
export interface RedwoodClient {
  embed<T = unknown>(opts: { input: string | string[] } & EmbedOptions): Promise<T[]>;
  generate<T = string | GenerationShape>(opts: GenerateOptions): Promise<T>;
}
```
kevin: we should also add a small compile/test matrix in CI: TS build with `isolatedModules: true`, bundle with esbuild (edge target), and a Node ESM build. If CI catches it we won't ship broken types again.
maria: CI just failed on the sample build when I pushed the reproducer — output: `TS1208: 'samples/edge-types/src/edge.ts' cannot be compiled under --isolatedModules` and later runtime: `TypeError: client.embed is not a function` for some ESM/CJS mismatch. Full log: https://ci.internal/redsdk/1234
ci-bot: Build failed — see https://ci.internal/redsdk/1234 (tests, typecheck). @sophie assigned.
kevin: @sophie please also add a small `samples/edge-types/README.md` that documents the recommended tsconfig for edge consumers and notes caveats (esModuleInterop, moduleResolution: 'node', module: 'NodeNext' for newer runtimes).
sophie: will do. i'll open PR #2421 in a bit with:
- replace overloads with single generic signatures
- add `types/compat.d.ts` that exports helper compat types for legacy consumers
- update sample tsconfig and add README
- CI matrix job for `tsc --noEmit` with isolatedModules + esbuild bundle step
maria: thanks — one more ask: can we add a short migration note to changelog so customers know to pin older SDK versions if they rely on the old overload inference? we should avoid a surprise and give a timeline for the typed-surface upgrade.
kevin: agree. add `BREAKING.md` if we need a quick callout.
maria: thanks y'all — appreciate the quick triage :thumbsup:
jon: fyi after the PR we should run a smoke-check against a few internal prod routes that use complex generics (routing/typed prompts) — I'll queue that.
sophie: PR opened: #2421 — tagging reviewers @kevin @jon. I'll keep updates in the PR, and add a tiny runnable repro under `samples/edge-types` so external contributors can test locally.
maria: perfect — that sample will also help customer support when users file onboarding issues. closing loop here.
